_what: Grounded-asserted drives after landing aurora's left-foot ramp (78ac6882). Build s4.debug.bin 845638.

rightward_CONTROL.start: x1000, settled to y557 y_vel 0, plane A, gsp +$600 sustained held right
rightward_CONTROL.verdict: STILL RIDES. y430 against y429 before the ramp — ONE PIXEL different, reported as measured rather than rounded to 'unchanged'. The ramp did not break the working direction.

leftward_from_the_right_ramp.start: x1200 placed, settled to x1192 y542 angle $F4 — on the loop's own right foot, not flat
leftward_from_the_right_ramp.verdict: THE CLIMB STARTS. $0A is one of the ramp's authored angles ($02 $06 $0A $0C), so he is demonstrably on the new surface. Peaks at y458 then loses momentum and slides back.

leftward_FAIR_RUN_UP._why: the first leftward start was on a slope while the rightward control got a flat run-up. This gives leftward the same.
leftward_FAIR_RUN_UP.start: x1350, settled to y557 y_vel 0 angle $00 — flat, plane A, gsp -$600 sustained held left
leftward_FAIR_RUN_UP.verdict: CLIMBS, DOES NOT CREST. Peaks at y454 and slides back.

the_gap.meaning: the ramp fixed the thing it was built to fix — leftward went from DEAD FLAT at y557 with no arc contact at all, to 103px of genuine climb on authored angles. It does not by itself complete a leftward circuit at $600.
the_gap._not_diagnosed: why the 24px. Candidates I have NOT separated: the left ramp is shallower by design (16px over 56px of run) so preserves less speed; the left arc may be steeper above the join; or $600 is simply under the leftward threshold where it is over the rightward one. I am not guessing between them.

_still_open: the leftward rule comparison (both crossover rules, leftward from a grounded start) now has a floor to run on for the first time tonight, which is what it never had.
